description:
Workspace V&V rule: methodology and results, both, in the doc comment where a reader meets the test.

What can honestly be checked here:
  - overall material balance closes (sum of cuts == feed) to a stated tolerance
  - cut boiling ranges land in the conventional bands (naphtha/kero/diesel/AGO) — a sanity band, not an accuracy claim
  - the pseudo-component slate reproduces the bulk API gravity it was generated from (round-trip)
  - black-oil correlation outputs sit inside their published validity ranges for the chosen crude

What CANNOT be claimed and must be said so: this is not validated against a real refinery CDU or a published assay-to-yield dataset. State the absence explicitly rather than letting green tests imply validation. No human V&V.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
Done — V&V documentation is in the test doc comments, methodology and measured results together, per the workspace rule.

What IS checked, with numbers recorded where the reader meets the test:
  * API <-> SG round-trip inverse to <1e-12
  * bulk properties in crude-like ranges (38 degAPI -> SG 0.8348, MW 206.5 g/mol, NBP 538.8 K)
  * a heavier crude (22 degAPI) characterises as heavier on all three properties
  * pseudo-component slate normalises to 1 within 1e-9, boiling points 390-825 K
  * CrudeCut bands tile the temperature axis with no gaps or overlaps
  * config validation rejects five specific mistakes, each with its own error variant
  * column-basis split fractions partition unity to <1e-12
  * the full column converges (38 it, 6.7e-7) to a MONOTONIC profile with draw temperatures 423.6 / 494.9 / 511.7 / 530.8 / 588.5 K

What is explicitly NOT claimed, stated in the module header and again in the test:
  * no comparison against a real CDU, a published assay-to-yield dataset, or DWSIM itself
  * the pseudo-component slate is a DISTRIBUTION ASSUMPTION from two bulk numbers, not a measured assay; two crudes with the same API and mean NBP can have quite different TBP curves and yields
  * no stripping steam, no pump-arounds, no furnace, no vacuum tower — the energy balance is not a refinery's
  * the CDU-band agreement of the draw temperatures is a SANITY check, not a validation

No human V&V is claimed.

title: crude: V&V — document methodology AND measured numbers

description: CLAUDE.md's README/Markdown rule mandates validating every README with 'pandoc -f gfm+tex_math_dollars -t html --mathml README.md > /dev/null' (or cmark-gfm as a structure-only fallback). NEITHER is installed on this machine, so the mandated check could not be run during the 2026-08-07 bookkeeping pass -- agents had to substitute ad-hoc structural checks (balanced fences, balanced backticks, consistent table columns, no unmatched $). That is weaker than the rule requires and silently degrades every future bookkeeping pass. Install pandoc (preferred, since it validates the LaTeX math too).
title: install pandoc or cmark-gfm — the mandated README validation cannot be run
